title: Mammalian-scale neuromorphic learning machine near biological energy

concept.text: The proposed innovation is a neuromorphic computing system that combines human-scale numbers of adaptive processing elements, continuous local learning and whole-system computing power comparable to a biological brain while operating at biological timescales. Neuromorphic architectures bring memory and event-driven, spike-like computation together. The intended machine would learn from incoming streams during operation, without depending on a separate offline backpropagation cluster for that continuing adaptation.

Although the retained title says mammalian-scale, the proposed numerical goal is specifically human-scale: approximately 10¹¹ neuron-equivalents, with 10¹⁴ to 10¹⁵ synapse-equivalents as a proposed engineering target. Mammalian brains span a much wider range of sizes. Artificial neurons and synapses would need explicit functional definitions; counting them does not establish equivalence to biological cells, connections or cognition. A system assembled from multiple dies or packages could qualify. The defining advance is the combined capability and complete computing power budget, rather than placement on one chip.

significance.text: If demonstrated on meaningful streaming or embodied tasks, this combination would provide a substantial new capability: sustained adaptive processing at human-scale element counts within a biological computing power budget. Its significance would come from achieving scale, useful ongoing learning and low total computing power simultaneously. Efficient execution of a fixed, previously trained sparse network establishes a narrower capability.

Such a machine could also support experiments on large-scale neural computation: how distributed adaptive elements represent information, coordinate activity and learn over time. The reviewed supplementary material identifies testing neural computational concepts as an established use of neuromorphic systems. Expanding that substrate would not automatically produce a detailed biological brain model. Matching element counts and power would likewise leave human cognition and broad autonomous competence as separate scientific achievements.

Conditional downstream possibilities include adaptive controllers and autonomous devices whose computing subsystem can process changing environments within a tightly constrained energy budget. Their total power and operating endurance would still depend on sensing, actuation, communications, energy storage and other components. The biological comparison itself needs care: the supplied metabolism paper reports that the human brain uses approximately 20% of whole-body energy while accounting for about 2% of body mass. That fraction does not establish a measured 20 W electrical benchmark for a machine.

missing_breakthrough.text: The central integration challenge is to make very large numbers of adaptive elements communicate and learn continuously while preserving useful performance and a brain-comparable computing power budget. Existing evidence establishes architectural foundations and online-learning progress, but does not demonstrate this complete combination. The January 2025 review's accessible abstract discusses scaling challenges; its reviewed supplement describes algorithms and hardware implementations that support online learning. The missing capability therefore cannot be reduced to an absence of local-learning methods.

Engineering synthesis: the hardware must accommodate the proposed adaptive state and connectivity while keeping memory access, spike routing, synchronization and learning updates within the total power budget. Scaling element counts alone would be insufficient if communication congestion, insufficient connectivity or slow updates prevented useful operation at the declared biological rates. Multiple dies and packages remain acceptable, but their interconnects and supporting equipment must fit the same performance and power requirements.

Scientific and engineering synthesis: local update rules must produce useful adaptation across changing streams, retain earlier capabilities and avoid unstable activity or destructive interference. A scalable software and measurement stack must expose those learning behaviors and account for all supporting computation. These are concrete requirements of the proposed machine, rather than findings established in detail by the retained Nature main article: the supplied review had access only to its subscription preview and complete supplement.

current_state.text: In its April 17, 2024 announcement, Intel described Hala Point as the world's largest neuromorphic system. Intel reported capacity for up to 1.15 billion neurons and 128 billion synapses across 140,544 neuromorphic processing cores, with maximum system power of 2,600 W. It compared the neuron capacity with an owl brain or the cortex of a capuchin monkey. These are dated vendor-reported specifications and capacity analogies, rather than independent verification of human-scale continuous learning at biological power. The maximum-power figure does not specify consumption during a particular learning workload or at a particular biological spike rate.

The 2009 human-brain review reports an estimate of approximately 86 billion neurons and 85 billion non-neuronal cells in adult male brains. Relative to that neuron estimate, Hala Point's reported capacity is about 75 times smaller. Intel also reported that its full neuron capacity could execute up to 20 times faster than a human brain and stated that Hala Point was not intended for neuroscience modeling. These comparisons do not make its simplified neuron models functionally equivalent to biological neurons; dividing its watts by neuron capacity and comparing the result directly with human metabolism would obscure differences in models, workloads and operating rates.

Intel's reported efficiency of 15 TOPS/W concerned a sparse 8-bit deep-network workload. The characterized multilayer perceptron used 10:1 pruning sparsity and sigma-delta neuron models with 10% activation rates. This is relevant evidence of selected-workload efficiency, but it does not establish continuous local learning at the proposed scale and whole-system biological power. The announcement presented large-scale real-time continuous learning as a future possibility.

The January 22, 2025 Nature review, Neuromorphic computing at scale, supplies additional evidence of progress through its reviewed supplementary document. That supplement describes DECOLLE, e-prop and hardware implementations supporting online learning, together with progress toward continual learning. It also reports that SpiNNaker-2, released in 2022, was undergoing expansion toward 720 boards and a target of 5.2 billion neurons. The expansion is a reported target, not evidence that the larger system was completed. The retained main article is a subscription preview; the complete supplementary document does not substitute for access to the main technical discussion.

The supplied evidence does not establish the largest neuromorphic system as of November 1, 2026, or whether any later system has achieved the complete proposed combination. The supplied review contains no freshness search record capable of settling those questions. This limits present-day conclusions; it does not invalidate the dated Hala Point specifications or establish that later advances did not occur.

completion_criteria.text: Proposed scale criterion: demonstrate an operational system with on the order of 10¹¹ neuron-equivalents, anchored to the reported human estimate of approximately 86 billion neurons, and 10¹⁴ to 10¹⁵ synapse-equivalents. The synapse range is a proposed engineering target; the supplied sources do not establish its proximity to the human whole-brain synapse count. Before testing, define each equivalent's state, dynamics, precision, connectivity and learning capability, and distinguish provisioned capacity from elements actively participating in the demonstration. These are proposed criteria, not established standards.
completion_criteria.label: Operational system of order 10¹¹ neuron-equivalents and 10¹⁴–10¹⁵ synapse-equivalents

completion_criteria.text: Proposed power criterion: measure complete computing-system power while the system performs the declared learning workload at specified biological spike rates and response times. Set an explicit watt threshold with a stated biological and measurement basis before testing; the supplied metabolic energy fraction alone cannot determine it. The proposed measurement boundary should account for memory, interconnects, host support, power conversion and cooling needed to sustain operation. Report the power of sensors and actuators separately if the demonstration uses a robot.
completion_criteria.label: Complete-system power during biological-rate learning meets a preset watt threshold

completion_criteria.text: Proposed learning criterion: demonstrate useful continuous local adaptation on streaming or embodied tasks without relying on a separate offline backpropagation cluster for that adaptation. Specify operating duration, incoming data rate, task changes, learning quality, retention of earlier capabilities and recovery from interference. Disclose any pretraining, external computation or periodic retraining so that the demonstrated contribution of local learning is clear. A sparse-network throughput or TOPS/W result alone would not satisfy this combined criterion.
completion_criteria.label: Useful continuous local streaming or embodied adaptation without offline backpropagation

completion_criteria.text: Proposed reproducibility criterion: publish sufficient hardware definitions, learning rules, workloads, configurations and power-measurement procedures for independent teams to reproduce the core results. Repeat measurements across declared activity levels and task changes, and report failures and practical limits alongside successes. Multiple dies or packages may qualify if their complete computing system meets the criteria. Finite experiments would establish demonstrated breadth over those conditions, rather than universal learning ability, human cognition or biological fidelity.
completion_criteria.label: Independent reproduction across activity levels and task changes, reporting limits

related_concepts.text: Roster-based synthesis: CPE-03, General-purpose fabric that retires data-movement dominance, has the closest architectural overlap because neuromorphic systems integrate memory and computation. CPE-05 specifically requires continuous adaptive learning at human-scale element counts and biological computing power. Success on those requirements would not by itself establish a general-purpose solution to data-movement dominance, while a successful CPE-03 fabric need not implement spiking computation or local learning.

Roster-based synthesis: CPE-02, Room-temperature general-purpose adiabatic reversible computer, and CPE-06, Wall-plug-superior superconducting classical computer at useful scale, share an interest in computing energy. Their defining advances concern different physical computing approaches and efficiency conditions. CPE-05 does not require reversible or superconducting operation, and either approach would still need to demonstrate the specified learning, scale and total computing power to satisfy CPE-05.

Roster-based synthesis: CPE-04, Cascadable general-purpose photonic computer with optical memory, could overlap through possible communication, memory or processing substrates. CPE-08, Economically manufacturable atomic-density defect-tolerant digital computer, could overlap through dense adaptive-state storage or computation. Neither roster entry's defining physical or manufacturing capability entails continuous local learning near biological energy. Conversely, CPE-05 does not require optical memory or atomic-density digital construction.

Roster-based synthesis: CPE-01, Application-scale fault-tolerant quantum computer, concerns reliable quantum computation; CPE-07, Utility-scale quantum-repeater internet, concerns quantum networking. Neither capability is a requirement of the proposed neuromorphic learning machine, and achieving CPE-05 would not establish either quantum capability. All remain distinct entries.

CPE-05 also overlaps continual-learning algorithms, robotics and computational neuroscience. Algorithms supply adaptation mechanisms, robotics supplies demanding streams of sensing and action, and neuroscience supplies computational questions and biological reference points. The defining contribution here is their integration through computing hardware, memory, communication and learning systems. The research's reference to historical item 4 cannot be matched confidently to another concept because that historical item was not supplied.

change_log.reason: Mammalian brains span many sizes; the approximately 10¹¹-neuron target is anchored to the supplied human estimate.

change_log.reason: A dated vendor announcement supports one system's capacity and maximum power, not a 2026 ranking or a power claim about all neuromorphic systems.

change_log.change: Integrated Hala Point's neuron, synapse, core, speed and workload details with limits on biological comparisons.
change_log.reason: These details explain the demonstrated scale and efficiency without treating artificial neuron capacity as biological or cognitive equivalence.

change_log.change: Distinguished demonstrated online-learning progress from the proposed integrated continuous-learning capability.
change_log.reason: The reviewed Nature supplement describes online-learning algorithms and implementations; claiming that local learning is absent would discard relevant progress.

change_log.change: Preserved the Nature access limitation and separated the SpiNNaker-2 expansion target from a completed demonstration.
change_log.reason: The main article was available only as a preview, and a planned 5.2-billion-neuron system does not establish its completion.

change_log.change: Recast the synapse range as a proposed engineering target and removed an implied verified 20 W benchmark.
change_log.reason: The supplied sources establish neither the claimed human synapse-count proximity nor a measured electrical watt threshold.

change_log.change: Separated direct adaptive-computing consequences from conditional robotics, cognition and neuroscience outcomes.
change_log.reason: Computing power does not determine total robot endurance, and element counts do not establish human cognition or detailed biological fidelity.

change_log.change: Expanded proposed completion demonstrations to cover equivalence, active capacity, learning quality, retention, operating conditions, power boundaries and reproducibility.
change_log.reason: The integrated goal needs testable conditions without presenting proposed thresholds as consensus standards or finite tests as universal proof.

change_log.change: Explained distinctions with every other supplied roster entry and retained uncertainty about historical item 4.
change_log.reason: The roster supports conceptual comparisons, but the absent historical item cannot support a verified identity or packaging requirement.

unresolved_issues: Whether any system achieved the complete proposed combination by November 1, 2026, and which system then had the largest relevant capacity, remain unresolved because the supplied freshness search record is empty.

The retained Nature main article is a subscription preview. Its detailed software and local-learning analysis, including the candidate's proposed quotation, could not be verified from that preview; the complete supplement supports narrower conclusions.
Artificial neuron and synapse equivalence, required connectivity and the relationship between provisioned capacity and actively useful adaptive elements still require operational definitions.
The proposed 10¹⁴ to 10¹⁵ synapse-equivalent range lacks a supplied biological whole-brain synapse-count anchor.
A numerical biological-power threshold and its measurement boundary remain to be justified; approximately 20% of whole-body energy use does not alone specify electrical watts.
Learning-quality, retention, duration and task-breadth thresholds remain proposals requiring explicit selection before a convincing demonstration.
The supplied record does not independently verify every vendor performance claim or establish Hala Point's power during a specified continuous-learning workload.
Historical item 4 was not supplied, so its identity and alleged single-chip or single-package requirement cannot be verified.

brief.title: A computer that keeps learning on a brain’s energy budget
possible: Robots and other self-operating devices could keep adapting to changing surroundings within a tightly limited computing energy budget. They would learn from incoming information during use, without sending that continuing learning to a separate training computer.
Their computers would combine human-scale numbers of adaptive processing units with power use comparable to a brain, while responding at biological speeds.
why: For autonomous devices, this would bring useful ongoing learning into computing systems with strict power limits. The advance would come from achieving scale, adaptation and low total computing power together.
Researchers could also test how large networks of adaptive elements represent information, coordinate activity and learn over time.

sources.showed: This review reports an estimate of about 86 billion neurons, the brain’s signaling cells, in adult male brains. It also describes how cell counts vary across mammalian brains.
sources.quote: These studies also showed that the human brain is not exceptional in its cellular composition, as it was found to contain as many neuronal and non-neuronal cells as would be expected of a primate brain of its size.
sources.cited_for: It supplies the human neuron-count reference for the proposed machine’s scale.
sources.not_established: Matching cell counts does not establish equivalent computation, learning or cognition.

sources.showed: Across six rodent and primate species, estimated average glucose use per neuron stayed relatively constant despite differences in brain size.
sources.quote:
The estimated average glucose use per neuron does not correlate with
neuronal density in any structure.
sources.cited_for: It provides a biological basis for relating brain energy use to neuron counts.
sources.not_established: Biological fuel consumption does not by itself set an electrical power limit for a computer.

sources.showed: Intel built Hala Point, a brain-inspired computer that brings memory and processing together. It reported efficient execution of selected, previously trained networks.
sources.quote: Neurons communicate directly with one another rather than communicating through memory, reducing overall power consumption.
sources.cited_for: It demonstrates progress in the scale and selected-workload efficiency of brain-inspired hardware.
sources.not_established: It does not demonstrate useful continuous learning at human scale within a brain-comparable total power budget.

sources.showed: The review describes approaches to scaling brain-inspired computers. Its supplement covers methods and hardware that learn during operation, alongside progress toward retaining learning over time.
sources.cited_for: It supports the existence of learning methods and identifies challenges in scaling the complete system.
sources.not_established: Learning methods and expansion plans do not establish a working machine that meets all the scale, learning and power requirements.

shown: Intel reports that Hala Point supports 1.15 billion artificial neurons, simplified models of nerve cells. Researchers have also developed hardware and methods that learn during operation. The complete combination of human-scale capacity, useful continuous learning and brain-comparable power remains to be demonstrated.
missing: A working system must combine the proposed processing and connection counts with useful continuous learning and low total power.
Communication, memory access and learning updates must fit the power budget while keeping pace with biological activity.
Learning must withstand changing tasks, preserve earlier capabilities and recover from interference without a separate training computer.
Independent teams must reproduce the combined results, including all supporting computing power.

milestones.label: Human-scale processing and adaptive connections
milestones.explanation: An operational machine would have to reach the proposed counts of artificial neurons and synapses, their adaptive connections, with each clearly defined. This establishes working scale beyond installed capacity.

milestones.label: Complete computing power within a justified biological limit
milestones.explanation: The complete computer, including support hardware and cooling, would have to learn at biological speeds below a justified, preset power limit. This tests whether low power use survives scaling.

milestones.label: Useful continuous learning without a separate training computer
milestones.explanation: Local learning, where elements update using nearby information, would have to adapt to changing streams or physical tasks without separate offline training. Retention tests would establish lasting usefulness.

milestones.label: Independent reproduction across activity levels and changing tasks
milestones.explanation: Independent teams would have to reproduce the core results across declared activity levels and task changes, reporting failures and limits. This establishes how broadly the demonstrated capability holds.

uncertain: What makes an artificial neuron or connection functionally useful, and how much connectivity is required, remain open questions.
The biological basis for a numerical power limit, and the boundary of that measurement, still need agreement.
Convincing thresholds for learning quality, retention, operating duration and task breadth remain to be chosen.

page.title: Human-scale neuromorphic online learning at 20 W
page.definition: A neuromorphic computer stores connection weights beside neural processing and runs at least 10¹¹ spiking units, which communicate by discrete events, and 10¹⁴ adaptive weighted connections. It learns from incoming data using signals available at each connection, in real time and at ≤20 W for the complete computing system.

goal.need: Across six rodent and primate species, estimated glucose use per neuron varied by 40%; the human brain accounts for about 20% of whole-body energy use at 2% of body mass. NEUROTECH compares a 20 W brain with GPUs consuming several hundred watts and identifies power consumption as a constraint on embedded neural computing.

figures.caption: Intel’s reported Hala Point capacity and power
figures.note: Intel announcement published on 17 April 2024; not peer reviewed. Capacity and maximum power do not establish power consumption during continuous learning.

statements.quote: Neuromorphic computing aims at building systems where weights are self-modified through local rules.
perform difficult perception and control tasks while at the same time achieving significant energy savings.
statements.context: The stated purpose of the brain-inspired chip developed through the SyNAPSE programme.

statements.body: IEEE International Roadmap for Devices and Systems
statements.quote: One target for a biologically realistic scale is to target billions of neurons
statements.context: Section 4.3.1.1 discusses spiking-network architectures; Table BC4.3 specifies approximately 100 billion neurons.

completion.title: A human-scale neuromorphic system learns locally in real time within 20 W.
completion.criterion: One physical system operates an active network of at least 10¹¹ spiking neurons and 10¹⁴ adaptive synapses at 1 ms time resolution, advancing at least as fast as real time. Local updates from incoming data improve a prespecified task score relative to the same network with learning disabled, without separate offline retraining for that adaptation. Average electrical input is ≤20 W during learning, including memory, interconnects, hosts, power conversion and required cooling. Provisioned but unused capacity does not count.
completion.set_by: Technology Atlas; operational criterion assembled from separately published architectural and local-learning goals.
completion.basis: Searches of DARPA SyNAPSE, IEEE IRDS, NEUROTECH, DOE EES2 and neuromorphic benchmarking literature found no joint pass/fail protocol for human-scale local learning, real-time operation and whole-system watts. IRDS supplies approximate scale and timing targets; NEUROTECH supplies a 20 W brain comparison and a local-learning goal. The minimum counts, power cap, accounting boundary and task comparison are Atlas operational choices.

milestones.title: An electronic synapse changes its connection strength in response to neural activity.
milestones.criterion: An electronic synapse implements activity-dependent connection-strength changes. Analog/mixed-signal: Kuzum and colleagues’ 2012 paper demonstrated spike-timing-dependent conductance changes in phase-change devices with 75 nm bottom electrodes; the main text gives no device sample size. Digital: Imam and Cleland demonstrated spike-timing-dependent plasticity on Loihi in their paper published on 16 March 2020.
milestones.set_by: DARPA SyNAPSE programme, initial component-development phase; its published criterion covers electronic synapses.
milestones.threshold_quote: capable of varying connection strength between two neurons

milestones.title: A single neuromorphic chip executes a connected neural network.
milestones.criterion: One chip executes a connected neural network in hardware. Digital: the TrueNorth paper published on 8 August 2014 reports 1 million neurons and 256 million synapses on one chip, consuming 63 mW for 400 × 240-pixel video at 30 frames/s. Analog/mixed-signal: the BrainScaleS-2 prototype paper published on 26 March 2019 reports 32 neurons and 1,024 synapses on one chip.
milestones.set_by: DARPA SyNAPSE programme, published single-chip system-development stage; no minimum neuron count is specified on the programme page.

milestones.title: A neuromorphic system learns through local synaptic updates during operation.
milestones.criterion: Weights change through local learning rules during operation; NEUROTECH gives no accuracy, retention or duration threshold. Digital: Loihi learned 10 gas-sensor patterns sequentially from one training example each; a replication published on 16 December 2024 found limited generalization to separate recordings. Analog/mixed-signal: BrainScaleS-2 learned simplified Pong smooth pursuit in 10 experiments of 100,000 learning iterations each.
milestones.set_by: NEUROTECH Horizon 2020 programme, Deliverable D2.6, section 2.5, published local-learning goal.
milestones.threshold_quote: weights are self-modified through local rules.

milestones.title: A neuromorphic system exchanges spikes between at least two chips.
milestones.criterion: At least two neuromorphic chips exchange spikes as one system. Digital: Hala Point contains 1,152 Loihi 2 chips; on 26 August 2025, Zhejiang University reported Wukong with 960 Darwin-III chips, more than two billion neurons and 2,000 W typical power. These system specifications are announcements, not peer-reviewed measurements. Analog/mixed-signal: a preprint submitted on 3 December 2025 reports BrainScaleS-2 chip-to-chip spike latencies below 1.3 µs within a backplane.
milestones.set_by: DARPA SyNAPSE programme, published multichip system-development stage for electronic neuromorphic hardware.

milestones.title: An active network of 10¹¹ neurons and 10¹⁴ adaptive synapses learns locally in real time.
milestones.criterion: One physical system operates an active network of at least 10¹¹ spiking neurons and 10¹⁴ adaptive synapses at 1 ms time resolution, advancing at least as fast as real time. Local updates from incoming data improve a prespecified task score relative to frozen weights, without separate offline retraining for that adaptation. No power ceiling applies at this stage.
milestones.set_by: Technology Atlas; searches of DARPA SyNAPSE, IEEE IRDS, NEUROTECH and neuromorphic learning benchmarks found no joint full-scale learning criterion. IRDS Table BC4.3 supplies approximately 100 billion neurons, approximately 1,000–10,000 synapses per neuron, 1 kHz network time resolution and spike-timing-dependent plasticity. The minimum counts, simultaneous real-time operation and task comparison are Atlas choices.

not_found: Searches found no hardware demonstration combining the stated scale, local learning, real-time operation and complete-system power limit for either case.
No common numerical threshold was found for learning quality, retention or operating duration at human scale.

results.finding: One Hala Point system runs spiking neural network models across 1,152 Loihi 2 processors.
results.detail: Intel reports inter-chip communication and execution of spiking neural network models at the system’s full neuron capacity.
results.quote: Applied to bio-inspired spiking neural network models, the system can execute its full capacity of 1.15 billion neurons 20 times faster than a human brain and up to 200 times faster rates at lower capacity.

results.finding: One Hala Point system can execute spiking models using 1.15 billion neurons.
results.detail: The reported neuron capacity is below 10¹¹. Intel reports support for up to 128 billion synapses, below 10¹⁴, and does not demonstrate the required local learning comparison.
results.quote: Applied to bio-inspired spiking neural network models, the system can execute its full capacity of 1.15 billion neurons 20 times faster than a human brain and up to 200 times faster rates at lower capacity.

results.finding: Loihi electronic synapses changed weights through spike-timing-dependent plasticity in a 72-column network; synapse sample size not stated.
results.detail: Synapses were strengthened when presynaptic spikes immediately preceded a postsynaptic spike; other incoming synapses were weakened.
results.quote: Specifically, the weights of synapses mediating presynaptic spikes that immediately preceded a postsynaptic spike were strengthened, and the weights of all other incoming synapses, including those in which the presynaptic MC spiked at other times or not at all, were weakened

results.finding: In 144,000 PCM synapses, spike-timing-dependent weight changes enabled temporal correlation detection with approximately 0.1% misclassified inputs.
results.detail: Seven PCM devices represented each synapse. The experiment used a software neuron and hardware synapses.
results.quote: The synaptic weights are updated using an STDP rule; synapses that receive an input spike within a time window before (after) the neuronal spike get potentiated (depressed).

results.finding: One TrueNorth digital chip ran a connected neural network at 63 mW.
results.detail: The chip contained one million spiking neurons and 256 million non-plastic synapses. The network processed 400 × 240-pixel video at 30 frames per second; the power measurement was for the chip.
results.quote:
We ran the multi-object detection and classiﬁcation network on TrueNorth with a 400 ⇥ 240
pixel video stream (Fig. 3) in real-time— 30 frames per second, where one frame used 33 time
steps, 1ms each. The network used 3, 406 of 4, 096 cores, and we measured its total power
consumption at 63mW during operation.

results.finding: One digital Darwin3 chip executed a connected two-layer neural network.
results.detail: The authors measured energy consumption while the first layer fired spikes and the second layer received and processed them.
results.quote:
We mea-
sured the energy consumption of the Darwin3
chip when running a two-layer neural network,
where the neurons in the first layer can fire spikes
without inputs, and the neurons in the second
layer receive spikes and perform calculations.

results.finding: Neurogrid ran a recurrent inhibitory network across 15 Neurocores, with each chip receiving its own spikes.
results.detail: The network also connected neurons across chips; each Neurocore accepted its own spikes and inhibited nearby neurons through shared dendrites.
results.quote:
The recurrent synaptic
connections were realized by multicasting spikes from
each Neurocore to all others (including itself).

results.finding: Loihi 2 CLP-SNN learned 40 object-class tasks online, with one video clip per class.
results.detail: On-chip local weight updates imprint each newly allocated prototype once; the deployed system does not subsequently adapt that prototype. Feature extraction and label comparison occur off-chip.
results.quote: In the 1-shot setting, each method learned a sequence of 40 online learning tasks, each containing a single short video clip per object category, similar to class-incremental learning.

results.finding: BrainScaleS-2 learned simplified Pong smooth pursuit in 10 experiments of 100,000 learning iterations each.
results.detail: The mixed-signal chip updated synaptic weights on-chip using locally measured spike correlations and a reward signal during the experiment.
results.quote: By repeating the procedure with ten randomly initialized weight matrices, we show that learning is reproducible, with little variation in the overall progress and outcome.

results.finding: Mixed-signal ROLLS trained 128 output neurons to distinguish 2 image classes using local synaptic updates.
results.detail: A supervised teacher signal guided training; after training, the system responded selectively to car and motorbike images. The source does not report a classification accuracy.
results.quote: We trained 64 of the VLSI output neurons of the network to become selective to one of two image classes, and the other 64 to become selective to the other class, via supervised learning protocol.

results.finding: DarwinWafer simulated a mouse brain across 32 neuromorphic chiplets.
results.detail: The system uses an inter-chip network that routes spike packets across the wafer. The result is reported in a preprint.
results.quote: Application studies demonstrate whole-brain simulations: two zebrafish brains per chiplet with high connectivity fidelity (Spearman r = 0.896) and a mouse brain mapped across 32 chiplets (r = 0.645).

results.finding: Darwin Monkey is reported as a brain-like computer with 960 Darwin3 chips.
results.detail: The source reports a multichip system but does not state that the chips exchange spikes.

results.finding: Neurogrid used 15 Neurocores to exchange spikes in a recurrent neural simulation.
results.detail: Each layer was mapped to a separate Neurocore; spikes were multicast to the others, with neighboring layers accepting them.
results.quote:
Neurogrid was programmed to simulate a recurrent
inhibitory network with 15 l ayers (Fig. 19), each mapped
onto a different Neurocore. The recurrent synaptic
connections were realized by multicasting spikes from
each Neurocore to all others (including itself).

results.finding: BrainScaleS-2 mixed-signal prototype: 4 chips exchanged spikes.
results.detail: The measurement used three senders and one receiver, with spikes routed through FPGAs.
